name: Data Exfiltration
description: Confirmed or suspected data theft — staging, bulk transfer, cloud sync abuse.
initialKeyQuestions: What data was exfiltrated, and how much?
What channel was used (cloud sync, email, FTP, HTTPS, USB)?
When did the exfiltration occur, and from which host/account?
Was the data staged before transfer?
Are there indicators of an insider vs. external attacker?

initialNextSteps.action: Block the exfiltration channel and the account/host performing the transfer
initialNextSteps.rationale: Stop ongoing data loss before scoping

initialNextSteps.action: Quantify exfiltrated data: volume, file types, and sensitivity classification
initialNextSteps.rationale: Drives breach-notification obligations and downstream scope
initialNextSteps.pointer: Proxy logs, CASB file-activity report, DLP alerts

initialNextSteps.action: Identify the staging location and any archive/compression used before transfer
initialNextSteps.rationale: Staging reveals intent and the full set of targeted data
initialNextSteps.pointer: Endpoint triage: temp dirs, zip/rar/7z creation, recent files

initialNextSteps.action: Correlate exfiltration timing with user activity and access patterns

reportFraming.summaryPrompt: Summarize the exfiltrated data, notification obligations, and containment for legal and the DPO.

synthesisHint: This is a data-exfiltration case — prioritize T1567 Exfiltration to Cloud Service, T1048 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol, T1052 Exfiltration Over Physical Medium, and T1074 Data Staged.
